This integration brings into Gladys the last decoded values of the LoRaWAN
sensors of an application on **The Things Network** (the community edition
of The Things Stack) or **The Things Stack Cloud**: temperature, humidity,
pressure, light, CO2, particulate matter, soil moisture, wind, UV, distance,
battery, water leak and motion.

It reads the **official Storage API** of The Things Stack, **read only**:
nothing is ever sent to your devices (no downlink), nothing is changed in the
console.

> **Unofficial** connector, not affiliated with The Things Industries. The
> integration has **never been tested with a real** The Things Network
> account yet: your feedback is welcome.

## 1. Activate the Storage Integration (required)

Without it, The Things Stack keeps no message and the integration sees
nothing.

1. Open the console (for example https://eu1.cloud.thethings.network/console)
   and your application.
2. Menu **Integrations > Storage Integration**.
3. Click **Activate Storage Integration**.

Only the messages received **after** the activation are kept, for a limited
time that depends on your plan (see the documentation of The Things Stack).

## 2. A payload formatter for each device

The integration reads the **decoded** payload (`decoded_payload`). Each
device (or the application) needs a formatter (**Payload formatters >
Uplink**): the one of the Device Repository, Cayenne LPP, or your own.

## 3. Create an API key

1. In the application: **API keys > Add API key**.
2. Give it only the **Read application traffic (uplink and downlink)** right.
3. Copy the key (it starts with `NNSXS.`): it is not shown again.

## 4. Configure the integration in Gladys

- **Cluster**: the one of your application, shown in the address of the
  console (`eu1` for Europe). For a The Things Stack Cloud tenant or your
  own server, choose **Other server** and enter its host name (HTTPS only,
  for example `mytenant.eu1.cloud.thethings.industries`).
- **Application ID**: as shown in the console.
- **API key**: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again; sent only
  to the chosen server, in a header (never in an address), and never written
  to the logs.
- **Read interval**: 5 minutes by default (2 to 60). One request per read,
  for every device of the application.

Then click **Test the application**: the button shows the last values of each
device, the fields ignored and when the next read can happen. The devices
show up in the **Discovery** tab as soon as their first message is read.

## Recognized values

A payload formatter may name its fields as it likes. The integration only
creates a Gladys feature when it knows **what** the field measures **and in
which unit**, and only with the units Gladys knows. A value out of bounds is
left out (never clamped). Every other field is ignored (the test button lists
them).

| Measure         | Recognized field names (case, `_` and Cayenne channel number ignored)                                                  | Unit in Gladys                   |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Temperature     | `temperature`, `temp`, `TempC`, `TempC_SHT`, `TempC_DS`, `air_temperature`, `soil_temperature`, `water_temperature`... | °C (-50 to 125)                  |
| Humidity        | `humidity`, `hum`, `Hum_SHT`, `relative_humidity`, `air_humidity`, `rh`                                                | %                                |
| Pressure        | `barometric_pressure`, `barometer`, `air_pressure`, `baro` (300 to 1100 hPa); `pressure` alone: 850 to 1100 hPa        | hPa (a value in Pa is converted) |
| Light           | `illuminance`, `luminosity`, `lux`, `light`, `light_intensity`, `ILL_lx`                                               | lux                              |
| CO2             | `co2`, `co2_ppm`, `carbon_dioxide`                                                                                     | ppm                              |
| Particles       | `pm25`, `pm2_5`, `pm10`                                                                                                | µg/m³                            |
| Battery         | `battery_level`, `battery_percent`, `battery` or `bat`: whole numbers from 6 to 100 (then 0 to 100)                    | %                                |
| Battery voltage | `BatV`, `battery_voltage`, `vbat`; in mV: `battery_mv`, `bat_mv`                                                       | V                                |
| Distance        | `distance_mm`, `distance_cm`, `distance_m` (a distance without unit is ignored)                                        | mm, cm, m                        |
| Soil moisture   | `soil_moisture`, `moisture`, `water_soil`, `vwc`                                                                       | %                                |
| Wind            | `wind_speed` (m/s), `wind_speed_kmh`                                                                                   | m/s, km/h                        |
| UV              | `uv`, `uv_index`                                                                                                       | UV index                         |
| Water leak      | `leak`, `water_leak`, `leakage` (true/false or a whole number: 1 and above = detected)                                 | detected or not                  |
| Motion          | `motion`, `occupancy`, `pir` (true/false or a whole number, e.g. a count of detections: 1 and above = detected)        | detected or not                  |

**SenseCAP** sensors (Seeed) are read by their types (`Air Temperature`,
`Air Humidity`, `Light Intensity`, `Barometric Pressure`, `UV Index`, `Wind
Speed`...) and their battery. A formatter may also declare the unit of its
fields with `_sensor_attr`, as in Home Assistant:
`{"_sensor_attr": {"distance": {"unit": "cm", "device_class": "distance"}}}`.

The type and the unit of a field are chosen when it is first read, then never
change (after a loss of `/data`, the feature already created decides). A
feature already created is never removed from its device.

A bare `battery` or `bat` field is ambiguous: some decoders put a rounded
voltage there (3 for 3 V) or the LoRaWAN 0-254 scale. Only a whole number from
6 to 100 is first read as a percentage; once it gave a value above 5 %, values
from 0 to 5 % are read too (a nearly empty battery stays visible). Prefer a decoder that names
`battery_level` or `BatV`.

## How it works

- Each message is published **once**, in the order it was received: no value
  is lost between two reads (a leak 0 -> 1 -> 0 does reach Gladys).
- **Scenes**: the newest value of each feature, received since the previous
  read (interval + 2 minutes), is published "live": Gladys then runs the
  scenes, at the time of the read (so up to one interval after the measure),
  and the history dates it from the read. For a water leak or a motion, every
  change of that period is published live, in order. Older messages
  (catching up after a pause, a refusal or a stop) are published dated when
  they were received, oldest first: they go to the history without running a
  scene.
- Bounded catch-up: the messages of the last 6 hours, at most 48 per feature.
  At the very first start, only those of the last 3 hours.
- A device is identified by its **DevEUI** (or, without one, by the
  application and device IDs): a device deleted and created again with
  another DevEUI under the same ID becomes a new device.
- At most 100 devices (a device silent for 30 days and not created in Gladys
  is forgotten), 24 values per device and 1000 messages per read. A message
  over 256 KB is skipped (and counted in the status); an answer over 8 MB is
  read up to that bound (newest first): the status says so and advises a
  shorter interval.
- Gladys accepts 300 states per minute: the states leave in batches, within
  that budget; the rest waits for the next minute.

## Errors and pauses

- **Key refused** (401), **missing right** (403) or **application not found
  / Storage Integration not activated** (404): the reads stop, one new try
  every 6 hours, or at once when you change the configuration. The status
  says why.
- **Server busy** (429 or 5xx): a pause (Retry-After, else 5 minutes doubling
  each time, from 1 minute to 6 hours).
- Nothing reads faster than the interval: not the test button, a
  reconnection nor a restart. The time of the last request, the pauses and
  the refusals are kept in `/data` (never the key; only while a key is
  refused, a salted fingerprint of that refused key, erased by the first
  success).

## Limits

- Read only: no downlink, no command.
- GPS positions are not taken over (Gladys has no position feature for a
  sensor).
- Fields without a known unit (e.g. `analog_in`, `Work_mode`) are ignored.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt The Things Network in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your LoRaWAN application | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with The Things Industries. It reads the last decoded values of the devices of one application through the official Storage API of The Things Stack (The Things Network community edition or The Things Stack Cloud): temperature, humidity, pressure, light, CO2, particulate matter, soil moisture, wind, UV, distance, battery, water leak and motion, when the payload formatter names them. Read only: nothing is ever sent to your devices. Before anything else, activate the Storage Integration of the application in the console (Integrations > Storage Integration), then create an API key with the "Read application traffic" right. Never tested with a real account yet. |
| Cluster | `select` | Nein | The cluster of your application, shown in the address of the console (eu1 for Europe). |
| Other server | `string` | Nein | Only with "Other server": the host name of your The Things Stack (Cloud tenant or your own server), reached over HTTPS. |
| Application ID | `string` | Nein | The ID of the application in the console (lower case letters, digits and dashes). |
| API key | `secret` | Nein | An API key of the application (it starts with NNSXS.) with the "Read application traffic (uplink and downlink)" right only. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again; sent only to the server above. |
| Read interval (minutes) | `number` | Nein | One request each time, for every device of the application. Nothing reads sooner, not even the test button or a restart. LoRaWAN sensors usually send every 5 to 60 minutes. |

## So installierst du The Things Network in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: The Things Network erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-things-network:0.1.2`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-things-network](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-things-network).

The Things Network benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

The Things Network ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.

- [Alle Integrationen durchsuchen](/de/docs/integrations/), native und aus der Community
- [Deine eigene externe Integration bauen und veröffentlichen](/de/docs/dev/external-integrations/)
